findings.summary: New: the /free-audit form posts a second payload shape (leadType 'audit', website, source) to /api/contact via submitAudit. All client-side checks in FreeAudit.tsx:16-56 can be bypassed by a direct POST. If the backend accepts the payload loosely, or later fetches the submitted website to automate the audit, an attacker can supply an internal URL (for example http://169.254.169.254.x or an internal host): SSRF. Mail-header or HTML injection is also possible if the fields are interpolated into the notification email. The backend was not reviewed here, so whether it handles this shape correctly cannot be determined.
findings.fix: Backend (out of this repo): a Zod discriminated union on leadType ('contact'|'audit'). For audit: website z.string().url().max(300) with a protocol in [http, https]; source z.enum(['google','referral','social','ads','other']).optional(); the same name/email/phone/company/message limits as CONTACT_LIMITS; reject unknown keys (.strict()); honeypot non-empty -> silent 200. Never fetch `website` server-side without an SSRF guard (resolve, deny private/link-local/loopback ranges, no redirects). HTML-escape every field in the notification email.
findings.recommendation: Verify in the backend review before /free-audit receives production traffic.

findings.status: open (dormant: GA4 id is null; only reachable after Accept)
findings.summary: gtag('config') at :122-128 sets no page_location, and nothing calls gtag('set', ...) on navigation. Only page_view (trackPageView :168-176) carries an explicit origin+path page_location. gtag.js fills page_location / dl from document.location.href for every other event (generate_lead, cta_click, contact_click) and for GA4 Enhanced Measurement events, which are on by default for a new web stream. So the full URL, including query string and fragment, reaches Google. Attack or leak: an inbound link such as /contact?email=victim@x.com&token=... (an email-campaign merge field, a mistyped mailto, a CRM link), followed by a CTA click or a successful submit, sends that query to GA4. This contradicts the privacy ON-state promise ('we never send it your name, email address...', privacy.ts cookieBullets) and the runbook's 'no query string' claim (docs/ops/analytics.md section 2). The dataLayer itself is clean (reviewer probe: 0 PII hits). The leak is gtag.js's documented default URL collection, inferred from that behaviour and not executed, because no Google host was contacted.
findings.fix: In loadGtag, add page_location to the config: gtag('config', id, { ..., send_page_view: false, page_location: `${window.location.origin}${window.location.pathname}` }). In trackPageView, call window.gtag('set', { page_location: `${window.location.origin}${path}`, page_referrer: '' }) before the page_view event, so later custom events on that route inherit the stripped URL. Add a test: with location ?email=x#t, every dataLayer 'config'/'set' entry carries a page_location without '?' or '#'. Add to docs/ops/analytics.md section 1, as an owner step: in GA4 Admin > Data streams > Enhanced measurement, turn off 'Page changes based on browser history events', 'Site search' and 'Form interactions' (or turn Enhanced measurement off). Must be closed before C17 sets an id.

findings.summary: ga-disable-<id> is set on Decline, i.e. after gtag() has already been called. Google's documentation (developers.google.com/tag-platform/security/guides/privacy) says the property 'must be set before any calls to gtag() are made', while also saying the tag checks it before setting a cookie or sending data. So stopping gtag.js's own automatic events (Enhanced-measurement scroll/outbound click, user_engagement) after a same-page withdrawal is expected but not promised by Google, and was not executed against a Google host. The site's own sends are provably stopped (consentGranted), the Consent Mode denied update is sent, cookies are expired, and after a reload nothing loads, so the worst case is the cookieless-ping residual already described in A6-1, until the next page load.
findings.fix: No code change required now. Before C17 the owner must run docs/ops/analytics.md step 6.2 and confirm in DevTools that no collect request follows a same-page Decline (scroll included). If one is observed: either turn off 'Scrolls' and 'Outbound clicks' in Enhanced measurement (the site does not need them), or make a Decline that follows an earlier Accept call window.location.reload() after storing 'denied', so gtag.js is gone.

findings.summary: InlineText renders any href that does not start with '/' as <a href={href}> with no scheme check (:16-25), and anything starting with '/' through <Link> (:17-20), so '//host' becomes an off-site link. publishBlockers (src/content/insights/blog.ts:101-110) does not reject a link scheme, and the only link test (src/content/insights/blog.test.ts:107-108) checks hrefs that start with '/'. Executed probe (vite-node a7-postbody-probe.tsx): '[a](javascript:alert(1))' and '[b](JaVaScRiPt:...)' render <a href="javascript:..." target="_blank">, '[c](data:text/html,...)' renders a data: href, '[d](//evil.example/x)' renders href="//evil.example/x"; and a post containing the javascript: link is isPublishable()=true. React 18.3 only warns on javascript: URLs, and the CSP is Report-Only (public/_headers), so neither is a backstop. The input is repo-authored content behind owner approval and code review, not visitor input, hence LOW: the scenario is a pasted link from a draft or an AI-assisted rewrite that a reviewer misses, producing a script URL or an off-site link on a prerendered page. The site already owns the correct policy for untrusted text (src/components/chatbot/links.ts classifyHref).
findings.fix: In PostBody.tsx InlineText, classify every node.href with classifyHref (move src/components/chatbot/links.ts to a shared module, e.g. src/lib/links.ts, and import it from both): 'internal' -> <Link to={target.href}>, 'external' -> keep the new-tab <a> but allow only https: (reject http: and protocol-relative for posts), 'text' -> render node.text as plain text. Add to publishBlockers in blog.ts: for each linkTargets(post) value, push 'link target is not an internal path or an https URL' unless classifyHref gives internal, or external with protocol https:. Add blog.test.ts cases asserting that javascript:, data:, '//host' and 'http://' links make a post unpublishable and render as text in InlineText. findings.status: closed (fixed in addendum 9 delta; blog.ts:157-159 linkTargets built from parseInline; reviewer probe 13 mismatch strings, 0 disagreements)
findings.summary: The publish gate extracts link targets with its own regex /\]\(([^)\s]+)\)/g (linkTargets, :150-154) instead of the renderer's tokenizer (parseInline, :163). They disagree on overlapping brackets: for the text '](/ok[a](javascript:alert)' linkTargets returns ['/ok[a](javascript:alert'], which classifies internal, so publishBlockers is empty and the post publishes, while parseInline renders a link to 'javascript:alert'. The renderer's postLinkTarget turns that into plain text (probe output '](/oka', no <a>), so nothing dangerous reaches the DOM; the effect is that the gate can pass a post whose link silently degrades to text, and the gate is weaker than the docs (owner-content.md:36-37) say.
findings.fix: Derive linkTargets from the renderer: visibleText(post).flatMap(t => parseInline(t).filter(n => n.type === 'link').map(n => n.href)). Add '](/ok[a](javascript:alert)' to the rejected list in blog.test.ts so the gate and the renderer are proved to agree.
